previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman with primary central nervous system lymphoma, ulcerative colitis, asthma, and a history of DVT/PE was admitted for her sixth cycle of high-dose methotrexate chemotherapy. She tolerated the treatment well with no acute complications. Her methotrexate levels showed appropriate clearance, and she completed leucovorin rescue as planned. An X-ray of her right foot, performed due to ongoing neuropathic pain, was normal, and an MRI of the foot was planned for outpatient follow-up. She developed expected mild transaminitis and neutropenia, both monitored without intervention. Her headache was managed with acetaminophen and oxycodone. She remained stable throughout the admission, was discharged home with instructions to complete three days of oral leucovorin and sodium bicarbonate, and will resume mesalamine after leucovorin completion. She is scheduled for her next chemotherapy cycle in two weeks.

# CNS lymphoma: Received cycle #7 high-dose MTX 8g/m2 on 
___.  Creatinine clearance 104mL/hr.  She will require two 
more cycles at q2wks before switching to monthly doses per 
Neuro-onc.  Bicarb: 1meq/kg IV prior to MTX, 25meq IV with 
chemo, 50meq/L bicarb in IV fluids, 1300mg PO q2HR PRN to 
maintain urine pH >7.5-8.5 to enhance MTX excretion.  Followed 
MTX levels daily 24hr post-chemo.  Leucovorin rescue PO/IV q6hrs 
starting 24hrs after MTX.  Anti-emetics PRN.  Continued 
levetiracetam 500mg BID.  Continued acyclovir prophylaxis given 
hx of oral herpes. MTX level the day of discharge was 0.11, she 
continued to get hydration and leucovorin prior to mid afternoon 
discharge so she did not require oral leucovorin or bicarbonate 
at home. She is scheduled to return on ___ for cycle #8 high 
dose MTX. She will have two further Q2week courses of MTX and 
then a restaging MRI of her brain prior to consideration for 
less frequent treatment.
